input.quote: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 allocates IP in delivered Materials. Type I Materials are Customer-owned, but the default for any Material not expressly designated is Type II — i.e. IBM (or a third party) holds all right, title and interest even in works created during the Service performance period specifically for us. The only licence back is "irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up ... to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only", with no right to modify/prepare derivative works and no right to sublicense. That fails both the preferred position (Customer owns work product created for it) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business) on material terms. There is also no statement anywhere that we retain rights in our Content, Customer Components or data; §14.17 grants only expressly specified licences, so silence leaves our data ownership unconfirmed. No assignment of Customer IP or data to IBM and no joint ownership exists, so this is not walk-away territory. Redline: flip the default to Type I, extend the Type II licence to modification and sublicensing for our business purposes, and add a Customer Content/data ownership sentence. The broad licence we grant IBM in Type I Materials (p0084) is noted but not flagged, as it is not an assignment.

proposal.summary: Default deliverables to Customer-owned Type I Materials, broaden the Type II licence-back, and confirm Customer ownership of Content/data
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so we have made Type I (Customer-owned) the default for Materials created during the Services and broadened the Type II licence to let us modify and sublicense IBM's pre-existing materials embedded in deliverables. We have also confirmed that we retain all rights in our Content and data, which the Agreement currently leaves unstated.

ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
ops.newText: If not specified, Materials created during the Service performance period will be considered Type I Materials.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, distribute, modify and prepare derivative works based on, and sublicense, copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business purposes.

ops.text: Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright and all other intellectual property rights) in and to the Content and the Customer Components, including all data Customer or its Services Recipients provide or process through the e-business Hosting Environment, and nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers any such rights to IBM.
